title: U.S. House · South Dakota At-Large
area: Statewide, South Dakota (single at-large congressional district).

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Dusty Johnson (R) is not seeking re-election to the House and withdrew from this race, running instead for Governor of South Dakota in 2026. Marty Jackley, the sitting South Dakota Attorney General, defeated James Bialota 79.2%-20.8% in the June 2, 2026 Republican primary (Casey Crabtree and Dusty Johnson also withdrew from that primary). Nicole Gronli (also known as Nikki Gronli) advanced unopposed after South Dakota's Democratic primary was canceled. Jack Pittman (independent) did not make the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Marty Jackley
candidates.currentRole: Attorney General of South Dakota (2023-present; previously 2009-2019)

summary.text: Marty Jackley is the Republican nominee for South Dakota's open at-large House seat. He is the sitting South Dakota Attorney General and a former U.S. Attorney for the District of South Dakota, running on public safety, border security and support for the Trump administration's agenda.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the South Dakota School of Mines and Technology (1992) and a law degree from the University of South Dakota (1995).
Worked as a partner at Gunderson, Palmer, Nelson & Ashmore, LLP, and as a special assistant attorney general for South Dakota.
Served as U.S. Attorney for the District of South Dakota from 2006 to 2009.
Has served as South Dakota Attorney General from 2009 to 2019 and again from 2023 to present; appointed to the office in 2009 and elected to it in 2010, 2014, and 2022.

priorities.text: Public safety: backing police, sheriffs and prosecutors, drawing on his career prosecuting violent crime as Attorney General.
Border and immigration: securing the border and "finishing the wall," citing his prosecution of drug traffickers.
Supporting the Trump administration's agenda, including securing the border and cutting taxes.

positions.summary: Calls for securing the border, finishing the border wall, and says he has prosecuted traffickers who bring drugs across it.
positions.quote: Secure the border, finish the wall, and let law enforcement do its job.

positions.summary: Says the right to keep and bear arms is not negotiable and cites an A+ rating from the NRA.
positions.quote: The right to keep and bear arms is not negotiable.

positions.summary: Says he will back police, sheriffs and prosecutors with the tools and respect they have earned.

candidates.name: Nicole Gronli

summary.text: Nicole Gronli (also known as Nikki) is the Democratic nominee for South Dakota's open at-large House seat. She is a small-business owner and former state director of USDA Rural Development in South Dakota.

background.text: A small-business owner and rural Dell Rapids resident with nearly 30 years of experience in marketing, communications and leadership.
Led USDA Rural Development in South Dakota from 2022 to 2025, overseeing investments in rural housing, broadband, infrastructure and community facilities.

Has served on Dakota State University's Cyber Security Industry Advisory Board, as president of the Department of Defense STARBASE board, and as an appointee to the Minnehaha County Housing and Redevelopment Commission.

priorities.text: Says she is running to advocate for South Dakota and build "an economy that works for everyone."

candidates.researchNotes: Gronli's campaign site did not have an accessible detailed policy-positions page at the time of research (a linked "Priorities" page returned a 404); positions beyond her general economic message could not be documented from primary sources found.
